text:
Harper Lee: Hi finance  I charged a vendor on the corp card for custom hoodies for the team offsite: `EVENT SWAG CO 3,420.00 USD` on 2025-03-12. The vendor invoice is attached but it's a single line item. Marketing wants to split cost 70/30 (marketing covers promo items). What's the correct way to submit this and do we need a PO?

expenses-bot: Policy check: Branded merchandise > $500 requires vendor invoice and PO approval for marketing-sourced spend. Cost splits across departments must have approvals from both budget owners. If taxable goods, record sales tax where applicable. Please attach invoice and confirm GL codes and approvals.

Harper Lee: Uploading invoice now: [swag_invoice_031225.pdf]. Invoice total $3,420.00 includes printing + blank hoodies. Vendor is US-based, charged in USD. No PO was created because event was last-minute.

Jordan Nguyen: Hey @Harper  marketing approves covering 70% of the itemized printing line. I'll add a quick approval message here: Marketing sign-off to cover $2,394.00 (70%). We can invoice internal chargeback to Eng via our internal billing ticket. Do you need a vendor contact for an updated invoice with line-level pricing?

Priya Desai: Thanks @Jordan and @Harper. Two things: 1) Finance requires either an internal cost allocation memo or an updated vendor invoice showing split for chargeback. 2) For accounting, classify branded merchandise > $1,000 as "Promotional Expense" (GL PROMO-NA) unless the items are inventoried. If pieces > $250/unit we may need to treat as company property/inventory. How many units?

Harper Lee: Total units = 340 hoodies. Unit cost before tax = $8.50 printing + $1.00 blank hoodie = $9.50 per unit. So unit cost is under $250 each. No inventory tagging needed.

Jordan Nguyen: I'll ask the vendor for an itemized invoice showing unit qty and a split invoice (70% marketing / 30% Eng). They usually can generate two invoices or a single invoice with internal reference lines. I'll request updated invoice and cc finance@redwood.com.

Priya Desai: Perfect. Also confirm sales tax: vendor charged $120.00 sales tax. For the allocation, we apportion tax pro rata to each department's share. So marketing will be charged 70% of the tax. Please include tax breakdown on updated invoice.

Harper Lee: Noted. One more: the vendor applied a $45 "rush fee." Is that reimbursable? The fee was necessary for event timing. Manager @Jordan sign-off included?

Jordan Nguyen: I approve the rush fee as a one-time exception due to timeline. Approving $45 rush fee on behalf of Marketing for our share.

Priya Desai: Good. For submission: Harper, attach the updated vendor invoice or a short allocation memo signed by both budget owners to Ramp and set expense type to `Promo / Branded Merchandise`. In the Ramp notes include: vendor name, PO if created, unit count, GL code PROMO-NA, and internal allocation (Marketing 70% / Eng 30%).

Finance Ops: Once updated invoice is in, AP will split the payable per allocation and code journals accordingly. Reference for AP: EXP-20701. If vendor can't issue split invoice, we accept a signed inter-departmental chargeback memo and a single vendor invoice.

Harper Lee: I'll follow up with vendor and upload the updated invoice + Jordan's approval. Thanks everyone.

expenses-bot: Reminder: create PO for promotional orders > $1,000 next time when possible to avoid manual allocation.
